stem:
A heavy metal sphere of mass 0.81 kg is suspended from a string. The sphere is undergoing small oscillations from side to side, as shown in Fig. 4.1.

[[fig:f1]]

The oscillations of the sphere may be considered to be simple harmonic with amplitude 0.036 m and period 3.0 s.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text: State what is meant by simple harmonic motion.

parts.label: (b)(i)
parts.text: the angular frequency of the oscillations

parts.label: (b)(ii)
parts.text: the total energy of the oscillations.

parts.label: (c)
parts.text:
The suspended sphere is now lowered into water. The sphere is given a sideways displacement of +0.036 m from its equilibrium position and is then released at time *t* = 0. The water causes the motion of the sphere to be critically damped.

On Fig. 4.2, sketch the variation of the displacement *x* of the sphere from its equilibrium position with *t* from *t* = 0 to *t* = 6.0 s.

[[fig:f2]]

figures.caption: Fig. 4.1
figures.alt: A heavy sphere hangs from a string attached to a support, with dashed positions showing its oscillation about the vertical equilibrium position.

figures.caption: Fig. 4.2
figures.alt: A blank grid for sketching displacement x in metres against time t in seconds, with time marked from 0 to 6 s and displacement from −0.04 m to 0.04 m.
